analysis:
The supplied changes are documentation-only: docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (a date bump plus a new selected-model recovery section, with the head text units shown covering later parts of the file) and docs/architecture/model-autopilot.md (an added adoption-release clause, a selected-model recovery section, invariant 10 and a failure-mode entry). No executable code, wire protocol, key, attestation or cache-storage handling changes in these units, so no concrete regression against the threat model can be shown from the evidence.

The docs describe provider-local behaviour that touches A-018 (serving availability), TB-012 and T-059 (add-on hold). Recovery may evict adopted, unheld, idle models that meet an operation's victim rules. It never evicts a selected, pinned, held or busy model, or one a request could load straight back. An add-on hold pauses recovery and cancels an in-progress attempt. It releases an adoption ten minutes after the hold expires or the selected model began waiting, and never before min_dwell or per-model lease end.

Remaining questions for a later pass with the code (ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery.swift, ProviderLoop+SelectedModelPlacementPolicy.swift, isProtectedFromRecoveryEviction, selectedModelRecoveryVictimWait, enterAddonHold) are listed below. Neither pass has seen the code, so these are unverified contracts rather than findings.
- Whether recovery can evict a model while a Autopilot lease or placement protects it.
- Whether a coordinator-controlled hold_seconds or lease value can be abused to starve operator-selected models.
- Whether the busy-as-preload state interacts safely with coordinator preload and operation fencing.
- Whether withdrawing a released model as model_not_selected leaves in-flight requests safely finished.

No prompt-data, key, or encryption paths are described as changed. The hardware-support.md patch excerpt was truncated, so remaining new text in lines 371-408 was only partially visible.
